 Order
The petitioners are the accused Nos.1 to 3 in C.C. No.1203/2015 pending before the Judicial First
Class Magistrate Court Ii, Nedumangad.

The prosecution was launched on the basis Annexure A
complaint

submitted by the 3 rd respondent alleging violation of Section 3(1)(zz)(xii), Section 26(1)
& (2) (i), and Section 59(i) of the Food Safety and Standards Act read with Regulation 2.10.1(1) of the Food Safety and Standards (Food Products Standards and Food Additives) Regulations, 2011 and any other relevant Sections/Rules/Regulations thereunder.

entities.text: Food Safety and Standards (Food Products Standards and Food Additives) Regulations, 2011
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 2. The main allegation against the petitioner is that, the tea sold by the petitioner was found to be adulterated as it contained iron fillings beyond the permissible limits.
This Crl.M.C. is filed for quashing all further proceedings pursuant to Annexure A complaint.

3. Heard Sri.Benny P. Thomas, learned counsel for the petitioner, Smt.Sreeja V., learned Public Prosecutor for the State and Smt.Chithra P. George, learned counsel appearing for the CRL.MC NO.
5410 OF 2022 respondents 2 and 3.
4.

The specific contention put forward by the learned counsel for the petitioner is that, as per Annexure B Circular issued by the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India, the prosecution in all cases with the aforesaid allegations, cause of action of which arose prior to 19.05.2016, were directed to be withdrawn.

entities.text: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The reason for the same is that, even though the permissible limit of iron filling in the tea was fixed at the relevant time, there was no recognized mechanism for assessing the quantity of the same.
The learned counsel also brought my attention to the Annexure C order passed by this Court, wherein this Court quashed a similar prosecution by placing reliance upon Annexure B circular.
5. After hearing both sides and perusing the records, I am of the view that, the issue is covered by Annexure C order which in turn was passed by placing reliance on Annexure B.
The facts which lead to the filing of Annexure A compliant is exactly same and therefore, the proceedings initiated against the petitioners is CRL.MC NO. 5410 OF 2022 liable to be quashed.
